claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 16 and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 16, there are some additional eligibility rules that apply. To determine if you can claim Child Benefit for him, I need to ask:

Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any approved education right now. He finished his GCSEs and left school, but he has started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to clarify what type of apprenticeship Alex has started, as this is important for determining eligibility.

Is Alex's apprenticeship in England, and is it a formal apprenticeship program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, it's not in England actually. He's doing his apprenticeship in Belfast, Northern Ireland.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I also need to know a bit more about your living situation to complete the assessment.

Do you currently live in the UK, and specifically, do you live with Alex in Belfast?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. We live together here in Manchester - Alex just travels to Belfast for his apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have one more important question:

Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week as part of his apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

To summarize your situation:
- Alex is 16 years old
- He lives at home with you in Manchester, UK
- He's not in approved education or training
- He has started an apprenticeship in Belfast (Northern Ireland)
- He works less than 24 hours per week

Based on the UK Child Benefit rules, I now have enough information to make a determination about Alex's eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment of your situation, I'm sorry to inform you that you would be **ineligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally continues only if the child stays in approved education or training and is under 20 years old. You'll stop getting Child Benefit if your child starts an apprenticeship.

Since Alex:
- Is 16 years old
- Is not in approved education or training
- Has started an apprenticeship

He does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit to continue beyond age 16.

The fact that he works less than 24 hours per week doesn't change this outcome, as the rule specifically states that Child Benefit stops when a child starts an apprenticeship, regardless of the hours worked.

If you have any questions about this decision or if Alex's circumstances change in the future, please feel free to ask.

Since Alex has started an apprenticeship and is not in approved education or training, he would be ineligible for Child Benefit.
